s1.syndrome_frame: Painless scrotal swelling with testicular enlargement and solid masses
salient_findings: Large, solid masses in both testes on scrotal ultrasound
Tumor confined to the testis with lymphovascular invasion
key_facts: Scrotal ultrasound showed large, solid masses in both testes
Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin within normal limits
Serum lactate dehydrogenase within normal limits
No evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses on PET-CT scan
Pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types: small cells, medium cells, and large cells

shortlist.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with multiple cell types and lymphovascular invasion

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular enlargement and solid masses, although less likely given pleomorphic histology

shortlist.label: Embryonal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with small, medium, and large cells, consistent with embryonal carcinoma features

shortlist.label: Teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of multiple cell types, although less likely given lack of cystic components

shortlist.label: Yolk sac tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with potential for aggressive behavior, although less likely given normal AFP levels

shortlist.label: Choriocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pleomorphic tumor with potential for aggressive behavior, although less likely given normal β-hCG levels

shortlist.label: Sex cord-stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular enlargement and solid masses, with possible sex cord-stromal tumor components

shortlist.label: Leydig cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular enlargement and solid masses, with possible Leydig cell tumor components

raw.rationale: The presence of a pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types and the lack of elevated serum tumor markers are consistent with a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, which can be composed of multiple cell types and may not always have elevated tumor markers.

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Seminomas are typically composed of uniform cells and often have elevated serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin levels, which is not the case here.

rejected.label: Embryonal carcinoma
rejected.why: While embryonal carcinomas can be pleomorphic, they often have elevated serum α-fetoprotein levels, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Teratoma
rejected.why: Teratomas are a type of non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, but they often contain elements from all three germ layers, which is not mentioned in the case description.

rejected.label: Yolk sac tumor
rejected.why: Yolk sac tumors typically have elevated serum α-fetoprotein levels, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Choriocarcinoma
rejected.why: Choriocarcinomas often have elevated serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin levels and are typically aggressive with metastatic disease, which is not consistent with this case.

rejected.label: Sex cord-stromal tumor
rejected.why: Sex cord-stromal tumors, such as Leydig cell tumors, typically have a different histologic appearance and often produce hormones leading to specific clinical symptoms, which is not mentioned in the case description.

rejected.label: Leydig cell tumor
rejected.why: Leydig cell tumors are a type of sex cord-stromal tumor that typically produce hormones leading to specific clinical symptoms, such as gynecomastia, which is not mentioned in the case description.
